statement: the itemId argument is copied verbatim to the returned card's researchItemId; the parser never derives an id from the markdown
title is taken from the first `# ` heading, trimmed of surrounding whitespace
a `kind:` line whose value matches a Kind rawValue yields that Kind
in the Swatches section only `- ` items that pass color(fromHex:) are retained, in document order; malformed items are silently dropped
a Senses item of form `<sense>: text` yields a tagged note; the sense token is matched case-insensitively (`SOUND:` -> .sound)
a Senses item with no recognised sense prefix yields an untagged note carrying the whole item text
an Images `- path` item is resolved against cardDirectory into a project-relative path, with `..` climbing out of that directory
an inline ![alt](path) written as loose prose inside the Images section is harvested and appended AFTER the dash items
with no `# ` heading present, title falls back to the fallbackTitle argument
with no `kind:` line present, kind defaults to .other
markdown containing no section headings yields empty swatches, notes and imagePaths (never nil, never a partial parse)
a `kind:` value that matches no Kind rawValue degrades to .other rather than failing
parse(template(title:kind:)) recovers exactly that title and kind
text between the `kind:` line and the first recognised `##` section becomes body, with interior blank-line runs preserved
body capture stops at the first recognised section heading and does not swallow that section's items
a card with no prose between `kind:` and the first section yields body == "" (empty string, not a blank line)
an inline ![alt](path) appearing in BODY prose is NOT harvested into imagePaths — body images stay editable prose
an inline image with a `://` scheme in body prose is not harvested; remote URLs never enter imagePaths
an inline image inside the Images section IS harvested and resolved relative to cardDirectory, even when written as loose prose rather than a dash item
a `kind:`-looking line inside body must NOT overwrite the card's kind — kind is captured at most once, before any section
an empty document yields a fully defaulted card: fallback title, .other, empty everything
a whitespace-only document becomes BODY, because the structural-framing test is raw.isEmpty rather than a blankness test
a '# ' line with no title text is not a title (the trimmed probe collapses it to '#') and is kept as body
a SECOND '# ' heading is kept as body text rather than discarded
a '#' with no following space is not a title
an H3 ('### ') heading is neither a title nor a section and falls into body
section heading matching is case-insensitive
extra spaces inside and after a section heading are tolerated
an INDENTED section heading still opens that section, because structure detection runs on the trimmed probe
a heading with no space after the hashes is not a section
a repeated section heading appends to the same collection rather than resetting it
sections may appear in any order
the kind key tolerates a missing space after the colon and any casing of the key itself
a kind: line appearing after a section heading is discarded entirely — neither captured as kind nor kept as body
swatches are neither deduplicated nor case-normalised by the parser
a 3-digit swatch survives parsing unexpanded; expansion happens only inside color(fromHex:)
an unrecognised sense prefix keeps the WHOLE item text, colon included
an item beginning with a colon is untagged and keeps the colon
whitespace around the sense token is tolerated
a bare '-' or '- ' item is dropped from every section
dash-item images are NOT deduplicated against each other
an inline image IS deduplicated against an already-collected dash item, giving the two intake routes different dedup rules
an absolute path passes through resolution unchanged
a remote-URL dash item is skipped entirely
climbing above the project root is clamped rather than rejected: '../../../../x.png' resolves to 'x.png'
'.' and '..' segments are collapsed in place during resolution
an empty cardDirectory leaves relative paths bare
